Thanks for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions before we surface to ops: 

- Use case: clinical summarization where provider notes (avg 3.5k input tokens) are summarized to a 300–600 token discharge summary.
- Expected peak concurrent providers: 18–25 at peak, steady-state ~8–12.
- SLA target: we want 95th <= 1.2s for the generated summary (end-to-end) for normal days; for peak days acceptable p95 up to 2.5s, but we'd like guidance on fallback behavior.

Questions: 
1) How do your latency numbers scale with large input contexts (2.5–4k tokens) and 1k output tokens?
2) Can streaming begin before full context is encoded (we want token-level partials to show progress to clinicians)?
3) Any recommended concurrency limits or batching knobs to keep p95 under 1.2s?

Appreciate the quick turn here — Nora

Subject: RE: Demo follow-up — latency targets and long-context use case

Nora — great meeting, thanks for the clear requirements. High-level answers and an action plan below. Short version up front: long inputs (3–4k tokens) increase encode time and KV warmup; streaming is supported and we can start emitting tokens once the first decoder step is ready, but end-to-end p95 will be driven by input enc/attention + decoding time.

SLO guidance (empirical starting point):
- Baseline model: open-llm-13B-quant (example in demo) on Dedicated GPUs.
- Encoding penalty: expect ~250–450ms additional for encoding 3–4k input tokens versus 256-token inputs (depends on model kv-cache warmup and attention kernels).
- Decoding cost: ~1–1.5ms per output token at our tuned 13B profile; so 600 output tokens ~600–900ms decoding.
- Combined p95 estimate (single request, no batching): 250–450ms (encode) + 600–900ms (decode) + small overhead (~50–100ms) => rough p95 0.9–1.45s.

Streaming: yes — we can stream partial output as decoder tokens are produced. For large contexts that still means the first token won't be available until the encoder pass completes (or the runtime begins decoder with partial encoder segments). We typically see first-token latency of ~350–600ms for 3–4k inputs with our current kernels.

Concurrency and throughput knobs:
- Recommended soft concurrency cap per model replica: 6–8 concurrent inflight requests for heavy-context / long-output usage to preserve the p95 range above.
- Use autoscaling target based on 'concurrent inflight' rather than raw QPS; set scale-up at 70% of target concurrency and scale-down at 30%.
- Enable prefix (KV) caching for repeated patient templates — this can shave 30–55% off the encoder penalty for identical prefixes.

Fallback behavior for peaks:
- Canary to a smaller decode-config: limit max output tokens to 300 (fast path) then post-process with a background job for full summary.
- Auto-fallback to a 7B quantized variant when queueing delays exceed threshold (we can keep latency but expect some output quality delta).

Next steps (action items):
1) I'll drop a latency/SLO matrix and a KV-cache diagram to this thread (attached).
2) lauren — can you propose a Pilot POA (1-month pilot: 2 dedicated GPUs + prefix cache) and a pricing sketch?
3) Marissa — can you sync with Veridian's infra on VPC peering and KMS requirements; they mentioned PHI — we should propose Private deployment details.

Happy to jump on a 30-min ops review with your engineering leads; propose Wed or Thu this week.

— Vivek

Internal note (cc'ing Veridian to keep them in the loop): answers to Dan's questions and pilot proposal below. I'll own pilot POA and pricing.

Answer highlights for Dan: 
- Encode penalty trend: mostly linear up to ~3k tokens on our tuned kernels; we see mild super-linear behavior beyond ~3.5–4k when memory pressure triggers attention-path fallbacks. We'll call out safe operating envelope at 4k and design guardrails.
- Prefix cache: 1k-token prefix (float32 kv representation compressed in our quantized path) -> approx 18–28 MB per cached prefix on a 13B quantized pipeline; invalidation is per-patient (time-to-live configurable), and we support eager invalidation through an API. Cache hit rates above 60% typically give >35% end-to-end p95 improvements on recurring templates.

Pilot POA (one-month):
- Infra: 2 dedicated GPU replicas (instance type: rtx-40x large-equivalent), prefix cache enabled with 48GB host-side cache, VPC peering + KMS integration for PHI.
- SLO targets for pilot: p95 <= 1.25s for 3k in / 600 out, with streaming first-token <= 600ms.
- Observability: per-request token histogram, per-route p95, and sample prompt/response logging (redacted) shipped to Veridian's logging bucket.
- Pricing: pilot rate card (sketch) attached in SLO_and_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx.

I'll schedule Thu 16:00 ET and include marissa for private deployment specifics. Vivek — can you bring the technical lead to go over kernel/attention behavior?

— Lauren
